clue.text: Dull hair interlinked? It could be slept on

indicators.note: the two words are linked like chain rings, sharing the letter where they meet, so one copy drops out

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their tangled, lank hair could serve as bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interlinked' tells you MATT and TRESS overlap on their shared T, so only one of the double T survives.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded base of a bed, the thing a sleeper lies on.

clue.text: Spice girl seen around clubs

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed so it wraps round the card-suit letter

parts.note: Mae is a girl's name
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl is spotted around the nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice girl' reads as one of the pop group, but 'Spice' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is a spice made from the dried outer covering of the nutmeg seed.

clue.text: Got over a dungeon refitting wooden flooring

indicators.note: refitting suggests the letters are taken apart and fitted together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone got through doing up a dungeon by laying a new timber floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue and groove is a joint where boards interlock, the standard method for laying wooden floorboards.

clue.text: Act a part, and run round back of hall to record song

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here taken from the word hall

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A performer acts a part, running round the hall's rear to make a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: To role-play is to take on a character and perform as them, acting a part.

clue.text: Swap parts to disrupt arrangement

indicators.note: the word is split into two parts which change places, front going to the back

parts.note: to upset plans is to disrupt them

explanation.surface: Swapping parts around is a way to disrupt a system.
explanation.walkthrough: UPSET splits as UP + SET; swap the two parts to get SET + UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is an arrangement or organisation of things.

clue.text: What's central to Drake's extraordinary drama?

definitions.text: What's central to Drake's extraordinary drama?

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their usual order
what is central to a name is its middle letter, here from Drake

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A question about what lay at the heart of Sir Francis Drake's remarkable story.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged DRAMA gives ARMAD, and the middle of DRAKE adds the final A. The whole clue is also the definition: the Spanish fleet was central to Drake's famous exploits of 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada, defeated in 1588 with Drake as a commander, was the heart of his most famous episode.

clue.text: Once more broadcast about fuel

parts.note: re means about or concerning
peat is dug and burnt as fuel

explanation.surface: A programme about fuel is shown on air again.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat is a programme broadcast again, so something shown once more.

clue.text: Serving up cream tea with sundae ——male kids might have fun here

indicators.note: serving up food means dishing it out, so these letters are dished out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cafe serves cream tea and an ice-cream sundae where boys can enjoy themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CREAM TEA and SUNDAE plus M (male) are rearranged; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall of slot machines and games where children go for fun.

clue.text: Mark in exam's perhaps too awful

indicators.note: awful means very bad, signalling these letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A student fears their exam mark may be too terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a grade; it is a punctuation mark, the one seen in 'exam's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mark between 'exam' and 's' showing possession is that punctuation sign.

clue.text: Domestic animals cross over the threshold?

indicators.note: over signals that the whole run of letters is turned back to front

parts.note: pets are domestic animals
a rood is a cross, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Household pets wander across the line into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole of PETS + ROOD backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The step just outside a front door is the house's threshold.

clue.text: Painter allowed to pursue miraculous wedding scene

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow, so these pieces come after the wedding place

parts.note: Cana is where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A painter is allowed to depict a famous wedding miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was an 18th-century Venetian painter famous for his views of Venice.

clue.text: Dog star or another heavenly body

definitions.meaning: the famous cartoon dog of Disney films, a canine celebrity
a dwarf planet in the outer solar system, formerly the ninth planet

explanation.definitionFit: Pluto is both Mickey Mouse's dog and a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun.

clue.text: One shouldn't start to hit a sleeping policeman

indicators.note: the word is not allowed its first letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to thump is to hit

explanation.surface: A warning that one shouldn't begin hitting a police officer who has nodded off.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping policeman is British slang for a speed bump across a road; the surface pictures a dozing officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hump is the raised strip in the road that the British call a sleeping policeman.

clue.text: Unchanging football pools arrangement's concerning

parts.note: a perm (permutation) is a combination of matches chosen on the British football pools betting coupon
anent is an old word for concerning

explanation.surface: Someone's football pools entry is always the same selection of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools is a British weekly betting game predicting match results; a perm covers many combinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent means lasting and not subject to change.

clue.text: A lot of soldiers might be required to empty this biggest shell?

definitions.text: A lot of soldiers might be required to empty this biggest shell?

parts.words: A lot of soldiers might be required to empty this biggest shell?
parts.note: soldiers here are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg; the largest bird lays the largest egg, needing a great many

explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are British breakfast toast fingers for dipping in a soft-boiled egg, not troops; the 'shell' is not artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest bird in the world lays the biggest egg of any living creature.

clue.text: Play with cast and a title, that's produced drippily in a cave

definitions.text: that's produced drippily in a cave

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle with it, moving the letters about

explanation.surface: A theatre production is being staged with its cast and a title, dripping with sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalactite is a mineral spike hanging from a cave roof, built up by dripping water.

clue.text: Showing leniency towards the French harangue

parts.note: to means towards
le is French for the
a rant is a harangue

explanation.surface: Being lenient towards the French despite a ranting tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tolerant is forgiving and lenient towards others.

clue.text: Ban a set of executive toys

indicators.note: a set of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone calls for a prohibition on a set of desk gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is an official ban or refusal of a proposal.

clue.text: Airport serving Laurel's Heath, perhaps?

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the thin half of Laurel and Hardy; with the possessive S
Ted Heath was a British Prime Minister, so Ted is an example of a Heath

explanation.surface: Which airport serves the heath belonging to Laurel?
explanation.walkthrough: Edward (Ted) Heath was UK Prime Minister 1970-74; 'serving' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Stansted is one of London's airports, in Essex.

clue.text: Regretted turning back couple that's ill-mannered

indicators.note: the back couple are the last two letters, and turning them swaps their order

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having turned their back on a pair who were impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters of RUED are turned, ED becoming DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude means impolite, lacking good manners.

clue.text: Succeeded with edges, applying one quite small knitting manoeuvre

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
lips are edges or rims
a titch is a small person

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in finishing the edges with a tiny knitting technique.
explanation.walkthrough: Titch is British slang for a small person; 'with' and 'applying' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip stitch is a knitting technique where a stitch is passed across unworked.

clue.text: Like chapter finale to shift to a higher plane

parts.note: as means like
an end is a finale

explanation.surface: A chapter's ending is changed so the story rises to loftier levels.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise or move upward to a higher level.

clue.text: Perhaps team of sailors from Southern Ireland getting to Bordeaux might require this?

definitions.text: getting to Bordeaux might require this

parts.note: Cork is a city and county in the south of Ireland; a crew from there is Cork's crew
a crew is the team that sails a ship

explanation.surface: A ship's crew sails from Cork to Bordeaux and wonders what they will need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordeaux' looks like the French port the sailors reach; it is the wine, and getting to it needs a bottle opener. 'Perhaps' marks the crew as just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the tool used to draw the cork from a bottle of wine such as Bordeaux.

clue.text: Composer's abandoning new act for "The Gamblers"?

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving something behind, so a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Wagner was a German composer

explanation.surface: A composer gives up a new act for an opera called The Gamblers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' looks like a part of an opera; it is the thing gamblers do.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager is a bet, the act that gamblers perform.

clue.text: Usual standard of opera finally falling

indicators.note: the final letter falls away from the word

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini

explanation.surface: Standards at the opera are slipping at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual or expected standard.

clue.text: Idiot's just left in bed

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: An idiot has only just left their bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' and the 's of 'Idiot's' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a foolish person.

clue.text: Make a running hitch?

parts.note: a hitch is a marriage (getting hitched) made while running off secretly, not a knot

explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch' suggests a knot; 'getting hitched' means marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly in order to marry.

clue.text: Announced possible end to a joust when the light fails

indicators.note: announced means said out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a joust could end with a knight falling from the horse

explanation.surface: A herald declares a tournament over as darkness descends.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is dusk, the time daylight fades.

clue.text: Very eager to have things grand and tall and thin

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand (a thousand)
reedy means tall and thin like a reed

explanation.surface: Someone wants things that are grand, tall and slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy describes someone who strongly wants to acquire more possessions.

clue.text: Incline to stop living in what has been given

indicators.note: in places the word for dying inside the word for a gift

parts.note: a grant is a sum given
to die is to stop living

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to stop living on handouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope or incline.
